CHAPTER 03 / WEBFRONT

Creating the interface

Creating the project, installing dependencies and compiling the interface.

Notation conventions

Function names, types, commands, options and filenames appear in monospace, for example describe, wf test or main.cpp. Italics introduce a term at its definition. Code blocks give the fragments to enter; the preceding text states their location and prerequisites.

Creating the project ↓Editing the sources ↓Dependencies and type checking ↓

Creating the project

Enter the following commands in the WebFront terminal. They perform four operations in order:

  • wf create life creates example sources in ui/, without overwriting an existing directory.
  • wf init creates the project manifest.
  • wf install installs packages and records their exact versions in the lock file.
  • wf dev compiles the TSX file and opens its preview.
WEBFRONT TERMINAL
wf create life
wf init
wf install react@19.3.1 react-dom@19.3.1
wf dev ui/main.tsx

Editing the sources

Open life-project/ui/main.tsx and style.css in your editor. Whenever a file is saved, wf dev rebuilds the interface and updates the preview.

If compilation fails, a diagnostic is displayed and the last successful version remains visible. Use Ctrl+C to stop watching. wf build performs a single build without watching for changes.

Dependencies and type checking

Packages must be usable in a browser. Installation scripts and native add-ons are not executed.

The lock file allows the same dependencies to be restored with wf restore. On an already provisioned machine, wf restore --offline checks the cached files.

TSX compilation removes type annotations. Checking the types themselves requires a separate wf check operation.
